title: Computer Networks
description: Interactive Interview Revision Cheat Sheet covering the URL navigation flow, conceptual network models, transport protocols, core internet concepts, HTTP status codes, addressing, browser storage, and web authentication.

topics.title: What Happens When You Type a URL Into a Browser?
topics.explanation:
• Step 1: Read the URL — The browser breaks down the web address to identify the protocol (like HTTPS), the site name, and the specific page you want.
• Step 2: Find the IP Address (DNS) — The browser looks up the website's phone number (IP address) using saved memory or a domain directory.
• Step 3: Connect to the Server — Your computer and the website's server say hello and agree to talk securely (TCP Handshake).
• Step 4: Send the Request — The browser asks the server for the page content (e.g., "Please send me the home page").
• Step 5: Server Works — The server checks its database, finds the right data, and packs it into a response.
• Step 6: Download Files — The browser downloads the website's code, styles, scripts, and pictures.
• Step 7: Draw the Page — The browser reads the HTML and CSS, calculates where everything goes, and paints the final page on your screen.
topics.tldr: Browser প্রথমে URL দেখে বুঝে কোন protocol, domain এবং resource request করা হয়েছে। DNS domain name-কে IP address-এ convert করে। TCP connection শুরু করতে Client এবং Server তিনটি message exchange করে: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK। Browser server-কে HTTP request পাঠিয়ে বলে কোন resource দরকার। Server request process করে, দরকার হলে database থেকে data এনে response পাঠায়। Browser HTML থেকে DOM বানায়, CSS apply করে, JavaScript চালায় এবং শেষে page screen-এ দেখায়।

traps.statement: The browser always contacts a DNS server.
traps.explanation: No. The browser may already have the IP address cached. It only performs a network DNS lookup if the required DNS information is not available in cache.

traps.statement: For HTTPS, establishing a TCP connection is the complete connection process.
traps.explanation: For HTTPS, establishing a TCP connection is not the complete process. After TCP connection establishment, the client and server also perform a TLS Handshake to establish encryption, certificate verification, and secure session keys.

questions.question: What happens when you type a URL into a browser?
questions.answer: When a user enters a URL, the browser first parses it and performs a DNS lookup to find the server's IP address. It then establishes a connection, typically using TCP, and for HTTPS performs a TLS handshake. The browser sends an HTTP request, the server processes it and returns a response. Finally, the browser processes HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and renders the webpage.

topics.title: Why Do We Use Network Layers?
topics.explanation: Networking is divided into layers to make communication: Easier to understand, Easier to design, Easier to troubleshoot, More modular. Each layer has a specific responsibility.
keyPoints: Each layer has a specific responsibility

topics.title: OSI Model — 7 Layers
topics.explanation:
The OSI Model is a conceptual networking model with 7 layers.

-Application Layer: Provides network services to applications. Common protocols: HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, DNS, SSH.

-Presentation Layer: Handles: Data formatting, Encryption, Decryption, Compression.

-Session Layer: Manages communication sessions between devices. It can: Start sessions, Maintain sessions, End sessions.

-Transport Layer: Handles communication between applications. Common protocols: TCP, UDP. Responsibilities include: Reliability, Flow control, Error handling, Segmentation, Port numbers. Important Note: TCP does not simply 'break data into packets.' At the transport layer, TCP handles segments. Lower layers encapsulate the data into packets and frames.

- Network Layer: Handles: IP addressing, Routing, Communication between networks. Example protocol: IP. Routers mainly operate at this layer.

-Data Link Layer: Handles communication within a local network. Uses: MAC addresses, Frames. Common technologies: Ethernet, Wi-Fi. Switches commonly operate at this layer.

-Physical Layer: Transmits raw bits using physical signals. Examples: Ethernet cables, Fiber optics, Radio signals, Network hardware.
topics.tldr: Application Layer application-কে network service ব্যবহার করতে দেয়। Data কীভাবে format, encrypt বা compress হবে তা Presentation Layer handle করে। Session Layer দুই device-এর communication session manage করে। Transport Layer data delivery এবং TCP/UDP communication handle করে। IP address ব্যবহার করে data কোন network path দিয়ে যাবে তা Network Layer handle করে। একই local network-এর device-এর মধ্যে MAC address ব্যবহার করে Data Link Layer-এ communication হয়। Physical Layer আসল signal বা raw bits transmit করে।

topics.title: TCP/IP Model — 4 Layers & Model Comparison
topics.explanation:
The TCP/IP model is a more practical model used to describe Internet networking:
- Application (HTTP, HTTPS, DNS, SMTP, FTP):
-Transport (TCP, UDP - Handles communication between applications):
-Internet (IP - Handles routing between networks):
-Network Access (Ethernet, Wi-Fi - Handles network communication technologies):
topics.tldr: OSI শেখা ও troubleshooting-এর জন্য useful, TCP/IP বাস্তব Internet communication-এর জন্য বেশি practical।

traps.statement: The OSI model is what is directly implemented on the modern Internet.
traps.explanation: Real-world Internet protocols are generally described using the TCP/IP model, while the OSI model is mainly used as a conceptual reference for learning and troubleshooting.

topics.title: TCP vs UDP
topics.explanation:
-Transmission Control Protocol: TCP is a reliable, connection-oriented transport protocol. It provides connection establishment, ordered delivery, error detection, retransmission, flow control, and congestion control.
Flow: Application Data → Split into Segments → Send to Receiver → Receiver Confirms Delivery → Lost Data? → Retransmit if Necessary. Common uses: Web browsing, HTTPS, Email, File transfer, Database communication.

- User Datagram Protocol: UDP is a connectionless transport protocol designed for low-overhead communication. It generally does not provide connection establishment, guaranteed delivery, ordered delivery, or automatic retransmission. This reduces overhead and can reduce latency. Common uses: Online gaming, Voice calls, Video calls, Live streaming, DNS queries. Applications using UDP can implement their own reliability mechanisms if required.
topics.tldr: TCP reliable এবং ordered data delivery নিশ্চিত করে। UDP speed এবং low latency-এর জন্য ভালো, কিন্তু TCP-এর মতো delivery guarantee দেয় না।
keyPoints: TCP is connection-oriented, reliable, maintains order, and retransmits lost packets.
UDP is connectionless, lightweight, has lower latency, but offers no delivery or ordering guarantees.
TCP segments data at the transport layer.
UDP is preferred for real-time applications where packet loss is acceptable over latency.

questions.question: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
questions.answer: TCP is connection-oriented and provides reliable, ordered delivery using mechanisms such as acknowledgments and retransmissions. UDP is connectionless and has lower overhead but does not guarantee delivery or ordering. TCP is commonly used when accuracy matters, while UDP is often preferred for real-time applications where low latency is more important.

traps.statement: UDP is always faster than TCP.
traps.explanation: UDP has less protocol overhead and does not require TCP-style reliability mechanisms, which can reduce latency. However, real-world performance depends on the application and network conditions.

topics.title: IP Address (IPv4 vs IPv6)
topics.explanation:
An IP Address is a logical address used to identify devices and route data across networks.

-IPv4: Uses 32-bit addresses (e.g., 192.168.1.1). Structure: 8 bits . 8 bits . 8 bits . 8 bits. Total theoretical address space: 2³² ≈ 4.3 billion addresses.

-IPv6: Uses 128-bit addresses (e.g., 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334). Total theoretical address space: 2¹²⁸ addresses, providing an extremely large address space.
topics.tldr: IPv4-এর address কম, তাই ভবিষ্যতের জন্য IPv6 অনেক বড় address space দেয়।

traps.statement: IPv4 and IPv6 can communicate directly with each other natively.
traps.explanation: They are different protocols, so transition mechanisms such as dual-stack, tunneling, or translation may be used depending on the network architecture.

topics.title: DNS — Domain Name System
topics.explanation:
-Domain Name System: DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses (e.g., google.com → DNS → IP Address). Humans remember names like google.com, whereas computers route traffic using IP addresses.
Analogy: DNS is the Internet's phonebook (Name → Phone Number corresponds to Domain → IP Address).
topics.tldr: DNS website-এর নামকে IP address-এ convert করে।

traps.statement: If DNS is completely down, communication to a remote server is entirely impossible.
traps.explanation: Users may be unable to resolve domain names to IP addresses. However, if the IP address is already known or cached, direct communication may still be technically possible depending on the service configuration.

topics.title: HTTP vs HTTPS
topics.explanation:
-HTTP: HyperText Transfer Protocol transfers data without TLS encryption. Potential risks include data interception, data modification by attackers, and lack of server identity verification.

-HTTPS (HTTP Secure): Uses HTTP + TLS. It provides Encryption, Integrity, and Server authentication.

Important Interview Note: People often say 'HTTPS uses SSL.' Modern HTTPS primarily uses TLS. SSL is the older protocol family and is deprecated.
topics.tldr: HTTPS TLS ব্যবহার করে data encrypt এবং secure communication নিশ্চিত করে।

traps.statement: HTTPS means a website is automatically trustworthy or malware-free.
traps.explanation: No. HTTPS secures communication between the client and server. It does not guarantee that the website itself is safe or trustworthy.

topics.title: HTTP Status Code Categories & Critical Codes
topics.explanation:
-> 1xx Informational: Request received and processing continues.
-> 2xx Success: Request was successfully received, understood, and accepted.
-> 3xx Redirection: Further action is needed to complete the request.
-> 4xx Client Error: The request contains bad syntax or cannot be fulfilled.
-> 5xx Server Error: The server failed to fulfill a valid request.
topics.tldr: 2xx → Success, 3xx → Redirect, 4xx → Client Problem, 5xx → Server Problem.

traps.statement: HTTP 401 means you are not permitted to view the resource.
traps.explanation: Despite the name 'Unauthorized', HTTP 401 generally means authentication is required or invalid ('Who are you?'). 403 Forbidden means the server knows who you are, but you do not have permission ('Permission denied').

topics.title: MAC Address vs IP Address
topics.explanation:
-MAC Address: A MAC Address is a hardware-level address associated with a network interface (e.g., 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E). MAC addresses are primarily used for communication on local networks at the data link layer.

-IP Address: An IP Address is a logical network address used for routing data across networks at the network layer (e.g., 192.168.1.10). IP addresses may change depending on network configuration.
topics.tldr: MAC local network-এ device/interface identify করে, আর IP different network-এর মধ্যে routing-এর জন্য ব্যবহার হয়।

comparisons.title: MAC vs IP
rows: Usually stable, but can be changed/spoofed

questions.question: What is the difference between a MAC address and an IP address?
questions.answer: A MAC address is mainly used for local network communication at the data link layer, while an IP address is a logical address used for routing data across different networks.

traps.statement: A MAC address is always permanently assigned and can never change.
traps.explanation: Modern systems can use MAC randomization, software-configured MAC addresses, and virtual network interfaces.

topics.title: Cookies, LocalStorage, and Sessions
topics.explanation:
-Cookies: Small pieces of data stored by the browser. Cookies can be automatically included with HTTP requests when applicable based on their attributes and request context. Common uses: Authentication, Session identifiers, Preferences, Tracking.
Important security flags:
- HttpOnly: JavaScript cannot directly access the cookie. Useful for reducing token exposure to many XSS attacks.
- Secure: Cookie should only be sent over HTTPS.
- SameSite: Helps control when cookies are sent in cross-site requests. Useful for reducing CSRF risks.

-LocalStorage: Browser storage accessible through JavaScript (e.g., localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark')). Common uses: Theme preference, UI settings, Non-sensitive cached application data. LocalStorage is not automatically sent with HTTP requests.

-Session: A session-based authentication system usually stores user session data on the server. The browser stores a Session ID (usually as a cookie). The server receives the ID and looks up the actual user session data.
topics.tldr: LocalStorage JavaScript দিয়ে access করা যায়, কিন্তু HttpOnly cookie JavaScript দিয়ে পড়া যায় না। Session auth-এ browser শুধু session ID রাখে, আসল session data server-side থাকে।

comparisons.title: Cookies vs Session
rows: Server uses session ID to locate data
Can persist based on expiry settings

traps.statement: LocalStorage is completely safe for storing JWT authentication tokens.
traps.explanation: LocalStorage is easy to use but JavaScript can access it, so an XSS vulnerability may expose tokens. HTTP-only cookies prevent JavaScript from directly reading the token, but cookie-based authentication requires careful CSRF protection and cookie configuration.

topics.title: Browser Cache vs LocalStorage
topics.explanation:
-Browser Cache: Browser cache stores resources to improve performance. Examples: Images, CSS, JavaScript, Fonts.

-LocalStorage: Stores key-value application data managed directly via JavaScript.
topics.tldr: Cache speed বাড়ায়, LocalStorage application-এর data store করে।

topics.title: GET vs POST
topics.explanation:
-GET: Primarily used to retrieve data (e.g., GET /users). Query parameters can be included in the URL (e.g., /users?page=1).

-POST: Commonly used to create or submit data (e.g., POST /users) sending data in the request body.

Security & Limits:
 Note: POST data is not automatically encrypted without HTTPS. Also, there is no universal HTTP specification limit for URL length in GET; practical limits depend on browsers, servers, proxies, and infrastructure.
topics.tldr: GET data retrieve করার জন্য, POST data submit বা create করার জন্য ব্যবহার হয়। Security-এর জন্য HTTPS দরকার।

traps.statement: POST is automatically secure because data is hidden in the request body.
traps.explanation: No. POST data is not automatically encrypted. HTTPS is required to encrypt data during transmission.

traps.statement: The HTTP specification defines a strict fixed size limit for GET URLs.
traps.explanation: There is no universal HTTP specification limit for URL length. Practical limits depend on browsers, servers, proxies, and infrastructure.

topics.title: Session-Based vs JWT-Based Authentication
topics.explanation:
Session-Based Authentication Flow: 1. User Logs In → 2. Server Verifies Credentials → 3. Server Creates Session → 4. Browser Stores Session ID → 5. Browser Sends Session ID → 6. Server Finds Session.
Both browser cookie and server session store work together to maintain login state.

JWT-Based Authentication Flow: 1. User Logs In → 2. Server Verifies Credentials → 3. Server Creates JWT → 4. Browser Stores JWT → 5. Browser Sends JWT → 6. Server Verifies JWT.
The JWT itself represents authentication information. As long as the token is valid, the user remains authenticated.

Where Should JWT Be Stored?
- LocalStorage: Easy to use → Accessible to JavaScript → Potential XSS exposure.
- HttpOnly Cookie: Not directly accessible to JavaScript → Can reduce token theft via XSS → Requires proper CSRF and cookie configuration.
topics.tldr: JWT auth-এ server token verify করে। Session auth-এ server session ID দিয়ে session data খুঁজে বের করে।

comparisons.title: Session vs JWT
rows: Easier stateless verification in many cases
Requires additional strategy for immediate revocation

traps.statement: JWT automatically makes an application more secure than sessions.
traps.explanation: No. Security depends on the implementation. JWT and sessions have different trade-offs involving token storage, expiration, revocation, CSRF, XSS, and server-side state.

questions.question: What happens when you type a URL into a browser?
questions.answer: The browser parses the URL and performs a DNS lookup to resolve the domain name to an IP address. It establishes a network connection, and for HTTPS performs a TLS handshake. The browser sends an HTTP request, the server processes it and returns a response. Finally, the browser processes HTML, CSS, and JavaScript and renders the page.

questions.question: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
questions.answer: TCP is connection-oriented and provides reliable, ordered delivery using mechanisms such as acknowledgments and retransmissions. UDP is connectionless and has lower overhead but does not guarantee delivery or ordering. TCP is commonly used when reliability matters, while UDP is often used for real-time applications.

questions.question: What is DNS?
questions.answer: DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses so clients can locate servers on a network.

questions.question: What is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
questions.answer: HTTP transfers application data without TLS encryption. HTTPS uses HTTP over TLS to provide encryption, integrity, and server authentication.

questions.question: What is the difference between a MAC address and an IP address?
questions.answer: A MAC address is mainly used for local network communication at the data link layer, while an IP address is a logical address used to route traffic across networks.

questions.question: What is the difference between Cookies and LocalStorage?
questions.answer: Cookies can be automatically sent with HTTP requests depending on their configuration, while LocalStorage is accessed through JavaScript and is not automatically sent to the server. Cookies are commonly used for authentication and session identifiers, while LocalStorage is often used for application preferences.

questions.question: What is the difference between Session and JWT authentication?
questions.answer: Session authentication usually stores session state on the server and the browser keeps a session identifier. JWT authentication uses a signed token that the server verifies on each request, often without requiring server-side session state.

questions.question: What is the difference between GET and POST?
questions.answer: GET is primarily used to retrieve data and commonly uses query parameters. POST is commonly used to submit or create data using the request body. Neither method automatically provides encryption; HTTPS is responsible for encrypting data in transit.

topics.title: RAPID REVISION FLASHCARDS
topics.explanation: Quick flashcards for rapid revision of core concepts.

flashcards.question: What does DNS do?
flashcards.answer: DNS converts a domain name into an IP address.

flashcards.question: What are the three steps of the TCP handshake?
What is the main difference between TCP and UDP?
flashcards.answer: TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery. UDP has lower overhead but does not guarantee delivery or ordering.

flashcards.question: What is HTTPS?
flashcards.answer: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS, providing encryption, integrity, and server authentication.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between IPv4 and IPv6?
flashcards.answer: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses, while IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses and provides a much larger address space.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between MAC and IP?
flashcards.answer: MAC is mainly used for local network delivery, while IP is used for routing across networks.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
flashcards.answer: 401 → Authentication missing or invalid; 403 → Authenticated but permission denied

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Cookies and LocalStorage?
flashcards.answer: Cookies can be automatically sent with HTTP requests depending on configuration, while LocalStorage is accessed via JavaScript and is not automatically sent to the server.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Session and JWT authentication?
flashcards.answer: Session authentication typically maintains state on the server with a client-stored session ID, while JWT authentication uses a cryptographically signed token verified statelessly on each request.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between GET and POST?
flashcards.answer: GET retrieves data using URL query parameters and is intended to be safe/idempotent, whereas POST submits data inside the request body and is not inherently encrypted without HTTPS.

flashcards.question: What is the primary difference between OSI and TCP/IP models?
flashcards.answer: The OSI model is a 7-layer theoretical and diagnostic reference framework, while the TCP/IP model is a practical 4-layer architecture representing real-world Internet communication.

flashcards.question: What is the function of the HttpOnly cookie flag?
flashcards.answer: The HttpOnly flag blocks client-side JavaScript from accessing the cookie, significantly mitigating the risk of credential and token theft via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

topics.title: FINAL INTERVIEW TRAP CHECKLIST & STRATEGY
topics.explanation: A checklist of common interview traps and an answering strategy using a One-Line Memory Map.
keyPoints: URL: Browser parses protocol + domain + path
UDP: Low Overhead + No Delivery Guarantee
Cookie: Can be sent with HTTP requests
JWT: Signed token verified by server

traps.statement: 401 and 403 status codes mean the exact same thing.
traps.explanation: 401 means authentication is missing or invalid, whereas 403 means the user is authenticated but lacks permission.

traps.statement: POST requests are inherently secure and encrypted by default compared to GET.
traps.explanation: Neither GET nor POST automatically provides encryption. HTTPS is strictly responsible for encrypting request and response data in transit.
